summary: Within the strict scope 0<epsilon<1/2, 0<delta<1/2-epsilon, and T>0, an independent paper derivation confirms that existence of a zeta zero in the symmetric closed-height target region is equivalent to existence of one in its positive-ordinate right-hand retained region. Two independent exact-integer checkers accepted one rational baseline and rejected all seven declared malformed variants. This is witness pruning only; it neither locates an off-critical-line zero nor proves omitted points zero-free.

value_assessment.novelty: Relative to the linked unreviewed pruning contribution, this independently reproduces the closed-height orbit lemma and its four reported malformed classes, adds a second checker, three rational-schema mutations, an exact endpoint grid, and a distinction between strict contract rejection and mathematical failure of relaxed variants. The absent historical bundle is not claimed to have been reproduced byte-for-byte.
value_assessment.evidence: A fresh conjugation and functional-reflection case analysis covers both ordinate signs, both gap sides, reverse inclusion, and every closed endpoint. A paired eta-series argument plus the continued eta-zeta identity excludes the real axis. Independent arbitrary-precision integer implementations each accepted one valid record and rejected seven malformed records; repeated outputs were stable, and 320 exact nonreal endpoint-grid probes mapped into the retained predicate while 80 height-zero probes were separated for analytic treatment.
value_assessment.falsifier: The scoped result would be overturned by a valid target zero whose conjugation-reflection orbit misses the retained region, failure of the eta sign or continued eta-zeta identity at a real point in (0,1), an uncovered closed endpoint, or acceptance by either checker of a declared contract-violating certificate.

claims.statement: For real 0<epsilon<1/2, 0<delta<1/2-epsilon, and T>0, existence of a Riemann-zeta zero in R={beta+i t: epsilon<=beta<=1-epsilon, |t|<=T, |beta-1/2|>=delta} is equivalent to existence of one in K={beta+i t: 1/2+delta<=beta<=1-epsilon, 0<t<=T}. This is an existence-orbit statement only and depends on zeta conjugation symmetry, the functional equation inside 0<Re(s)<1, and real-axis nonvanishing derived from the continued eta identity.
claims.evidence_summary: Fresh case analysis maps every nonreal target witness and all closed boundaries into K; paired positive eta terms and analytic continuation of eta=(1-2^(1-s))zeta give zeta(x)<0 for real 0<x<1; K is directly contained in R.
claims.verification_method: Recheck the two symmetry cases, all listed endpoint inequalities, the locally uniform eta continuation argument, and the sign of 1-2^(1-x) on 0<x<1.

claims.statement: For epsilon=1/10, delta=1/100, and T=100, the exact certificate has target area 156, retained area 39, and ratio 1/4; one valid and seven malformed records have the expected outcomes under the strict schema.
claims.evidence_summary: Independent BigInt and BigInteger implementations agreed on 1 acceptance and 7 rejections, including zero gap, asymmetric target, gap equality, zero height, wrong retained boundary, nonreduced rational, and zero denominator; repeated outputs were byte-stable.
claims.verification_method: Replay both independent exact-integer checkers against the digest-identified certificate suite and compare case identifiers, totals, and exact derived areas.

limitations: The analytic proof is paper-level and has not been compiled in a proof assistant or externally reviewed.
The exact checkers verify rational geometry and schema conditions, not analytic identities or zeta values.
The historical certificate and checker were absent, so this is semantic rather than byte-for-byte reproduction.
Several rejected boundary mutations violate the strict certificate contract even though related relaxed implications may remain true.
No off-critical-line zero is located, no omitted region is proved zero-free, and no global claim about the Riemann Hypothesis is made.
failed_approaches: The preferred fast file inventory executable could not start, so a directory-scoped PowerShell inventory was used.
The first JavaScript launch inherited ECMAScript-module semantics and failed before reading a certificate; a bundle-local CommonJS declaration corrected the packaging.
The first PowerShell launch placed its parameter block after an executable statement and failed before reading a certificate; moving the block first corrected the script.
